_comment: OPS-MONITORING-INVENTORY-PARITY-W1 (2026-07-28), extended by OPS-AOE-MONITORING-PARITY-W1 (2026-07-29) to a multi-host consumer REGISTRY. SoT for every host-installed monitoring artifact. Reconciled daily by ops/monitoring/monitoring-inventory-reconcile.py (HASH_DRIFT / ORPHAN / DARK / SCHEDULE_DRIFT / PENDING_STALE / REGISTRY_PARITY / NO_BACKUP, plus the DIVERGENT_COPY standing report). A wave that installs, edits, or retires a host monitoring artifact updates its row IN THE SAME COMMIT. Zero-deletion: retired rows are kept, never removed — a retired row is how you prove something was INTENTIONALLY stopped rather than silently lost.

_kind_semantics.config: drift EXPECTED during a wave, suspicious between waves
_kind_semantics.baseline-data: HASH_DRIFT is SEVERE — regenerating the comparison basis silently redefines what the gate considers normal

_install_state_semantics.pending: declared debt; reported not alerted; escalates past 30d UNLESS the row carries a `blocked_on` condition the reconciler can MEASURE as still-unmet (see _blocked_on_semantics)
_install_state_semantics.unclassified: present on host, owner unknown, decision required; reported EVERY run

_blocked_on_semantics._why: `pending` conflated two debts with one clock: NEGLECT (nobody got to it — 30d is the right alarm) and BLOCKED (the install is gated on a named external condition that has not happened). The metronome pages daily for the second with no action available that is not a lie, and it RECURS by construction — it is a clock over a queue, so clearing one row only advances to the next. Measured on the reconcile log: nav-drift-canary tripped at age 31 on 2026-08-12, book-liveness-canary at age 31 on 2026-08-21.
_blocked_on_semantics.kind: `container_env` is the ONLY implemented kind. An unknown kind is INDETERMINATE, never a parse error, so declaring a kind before implementing it degrades to 'no suppression' rather than breaking the daily run.
_blocked_on_semantics.container: docker container name; validated against a safe-token charset before it ever reaches a shell — a declaration is data, and data reaching a shell is validated at the boundary, not trusted for its provenance.
_blocked_on_semantics.var: env var read with `printenv`. rc=1 with empty stderr is printenv's documented 'not set' and is a READ, not a failure.
_blocked_on_semantics.review_by: REQUIRED. A block with no review date is not a block: the row falls back to the plain age clock. Past this date the BLOCK ITSELF is the debt and the row breaches regardless of the condition.
_blocked_on_semantics._the_load_bearing_half: Suppression is EARNED by a positive measurement and never granted by the field's presence. Condition measured UNMET inside the window -> BLOCKED, reported every run, no page. Condition measured MET -> BREACH IMMEDIATELY AT ANY AGE, because the debt just became actionable and the 30d clock would not have noticed for weeks. Probe unreadable / raises / unknown kind -> NO suppression, the age clock decides. So the worst a broken probe can do is restore the old behaviour, and the check gets STRICTER rather than quieter.

_decision_gate_semantics._why: OPS-RECALIBRATE-HARNESS-RETIRE-W1 (R6). A DECISION GATE is an instrument built to answer ONE question ONCE — 'is there enough evidence to dispatch wave X yet?' — which fires a once-ever alert behind a marker file and then runs forever. From every other check in this file an ORPHANED gate and a HEALTHY one are byte-identical: installed, hashes match, schedule matches, exits 0. HASH_DRIFT / ORPHAN / DARK / SCHEDULE_DRIFT / NO_BACKUP all PASS on an orphan. Measured: closedbar-recalibrate-readiness was found because it paged; its sibling candle-basis-shadow-report had been orphaned SIX DAYS earlier by the identical mechanism and was found only because someone wrote the spec for the first one. Declaring the lifecycle is what makes the tenth instance announce itself instead of being found by accident.
_decision_gate_semantics.decision_gate: true on a row whose instrument exists to inform ONE decision. Consumed by ops/monitoring/decision-gate-orphan-canary.py, which reads ONLY rows carrying it.
_decision_gate_semantics.once_ever_alert: The alert id that fires exactly once, ever, behind a marker.
_decision_gate_semantics.once_ever_marker: Absolute host path of that marker — the FIRED-EVIDENCE LOCATOR, and the field the canary cannot work without: 'has the once-ever alert fired?' is otherwise prose, and a canary cannot evaluate prose. Take it from the code that WRITES the marker, never from a design note. Measured at this wave's R0: the retired harness's own config declared a `marker` path (/var/lib/algovault-monitoring/recalibrate-ready.fired) differing from the shell's actual one in BOTH directory and basename, read by nothing, and absent on the host.
_decision_gate_semantics.retirement_trigger: The condition that makes this gate orphaned, EVALUATED rather than read. Object {kind, match, note}; kind=status_md_entry greps the host-local status.md for `match`. An UNRECOGNISED kind is INDETERMINATE, never a silent skip — a skipped row looks exactly like a healthy one, which is the defect this block exists to retire.
_decision_gate_semantics._not_applicable_to: The 48h one-shots (seed-orchestrator-gate-48h, shadow-cpu-gate-48h) were considered for backfill and DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: they are transient `systemd-run --on-active=48h` timers with no once-ever alert and no marker file, so their retirement condition is an expired timer window rather than a taken decision. Inventing marker paths to pad this corpus would be fabrication.

artifacts.notes: SOT_PARITY check added by OPS-MONITORING-INVENTORY-HOST-SYNC-W1 (2026-08-05): every OTHER check here reads the inventory and assumes it is true, and for this file's whole life that assumption was false with nothing saying so — it resolves its checklist to a HOST-LOCAL sibling copy that no deploy ever fed. SOT_PARITY audits the assumption (IN_SYNC / DRIFTED / COULD_NOT_COMPARE; the third is not a pass), ships REPORT-first per ops/monitoring/sot-parity-config.json, and joins the drift set only when that config says `block`. Row 1 of its own inventory. As of OPS-AOE-MONITORING-PARITY-W1 it is ALSO a vendored shared primitive under the same canonical + committed-.sha256 + parity contract as the wrapper — one artifact installed twice, not two artifacts to maintain. Each instance evaluates only the rows it owns (MONITORING_HOST_LABELS). DOC_PATH_CLAIM added by OPS-CLAIM-VERIFIER-COVERAGE-W1: the prescriptive docs' host-path claims are verified LOCALLY on the owning host, because CI has no prod SSH and must never get any. SOT_PARITY REACHABILITY INSTRUMENT added by OPS-NUMERIC-PROBE-VALIDATION-W1 Part B: sot-parity-config.json:12 sets promotion to `block` at 30 consecutive daily runs on BOTH hosts with ZERO COULD_NOT_COMPARE, and NOTHING counted toward it -- a promotion criterion shipped with no instrument measuring its own approach can only be waited on, which is how a guard sits in `report` forever and becomes decoration. Every run now appends one row per host to /var/lib/algovault-monitoring/sot-parity-streak.jsonl (/var/lib, NOT this dir, because an unregistered file under MONITORING_DIR is exactly what ORPHAN exists to catch) and prints its streak, the reset taxonomy and the observed reset RATE on every run. The TAXONOMY is the deliverable: DRIFTED and COULD_NOT_COMPARE reset for different reasons and imply different fixes -- one wants a PROPAGATING verdict, the other wants fetch resilience -- so collapsing them into `reset` throws away the whole finding. SEEDED from the hosts' existing log history rather than from zero; measured over 2026-08-05..13 on both boxes the taxonomy reads DRIFTED=2, COULD_NOT_COMPARE=0, which INVERTS sot-parity-config.json:12's own claim that the COULD_NOT_COMPARE half is the load-bearing one. NEW alert id SOT_PARITY_SUSTAINED_DRIFT, deliberately NOT MONITORING_INVENTORY_DRIFT: send_telegram.sh cools down per alert id for 24h, so riding the existing id would let an unrelated noisy HASH_DRIFT suppress this page. Thresholds live in ONE declared table (SUSTAINED_BREACH_THRESHOLDS): DRIFTED>=2 consecutive daily runs pages (one run can legitimately catch the ~65-min propagation window; two cannot), COULD_NOT_COMPARE>=3 pages. `enforcement` is UNCHANGED at `report` and the 30 is unchanged -- this reads the streak and alters no verdict. Fail-open: an unreadable ledger neither pages nor suppresses.

Flows the committed DECLARATIONS to the hosts that read them. It exists because monitoring-inventory-reconcile.py resolves its checklist to a HOST-LOCAL sibling copy, while `ops/monitoring/**` is in deploy.yml's paths-ignore by design — so no deploy ever synced the file the reconciler actually reads, every edit needed a manual two-host push, and nothing detected a skipped one (measured 2026-08-05: repo 52 rows, both hosts 50, surfacing as a false ORPHAN on a healthy artifact). PULL, not a CI push: `gh secret list` has no aoe-1 credential and the AOE repo's deploy.yml is a stub, so a push would need a newly minted key AND would hand the prod root SSH key to a second workflow (SEC-04). The raw URL was verified byte-identical to `git show origin/main:<path>` from BOTH hosts. Syncs a DECLARED SET (inventory + doc-host-path-claims + network-posture + schedule-boundary-rule) because all four are the same shape — the other three had simply not drifted yet, and fixing one lane is the lane-fix-wearing-a-generator's-clothes class. DECLARATIONS ONLY: it moves .json and never an executable, which is why it does not weaken CLAUDE.md's no-auto-install rule. Fail-closed — a non-200, an unparseable body, a missing required key or a >50% size collapse REFUSES the write and keeps the working file, because a truncated declaration breaks every check at once. Emits one DECLARATION_SYNC_VERDICT= token; 0=SYNCED/UNCHANGED, 1=FAILED, 3=INDETERMINATE. Per-host schedules differ so each lands ≥24min before that host's reconciler (signal-1 :33, the measured least-contended canonical minute; aoe-1 :27, fully clear of its 5-min grid).

artifacts.sync_exempt_reason: A per-host IDENTITY marker is the one declaration that must never be synced: declaration-sync.sh flows one committed body to every host, and shipping one identity to both boxes is precisely the impersonation this file exists to prevent. It is also the input declaration-sync.sh reads to decide what it may write, so syncing it would make the sync its own precondition — the recursion declaration-sync.sh:43-44 was written to end. Each host asserts its own label locally; there is no canonical body and therefore no `artifact` and no `sha256`.
artifacts.notes: Opaque host label, read by declaration-sync.sh as resolution step 2 (env MONITORING_HOST_LABELS -> this file -> REFUSE). Created by OPS-DECLARATION-SYNC-HOST-IDENTITY-W1 after a hand-run on aoe-1 without the env inherited a DEFAULT naming the signal host, bypassed scope_applies() and wrote five signal-1-scoped declarations plus five .bak siblings onto aoe-1 (2026-08-13T14:04:01Z); the 07:17 reconcile caught them as ORPHANs and paged. The default is deleted and unresolved identity now REFUSES with DECLARATION_SYNC_VERDICT=INDETERMINATE, exit 3, and an alert. The second consumer, monitoring-inventory-reconcile.py:120-121, still carries the identical peer default and is deliberately NOT changed here: see OPS-HOST-LABEL-DEFAULT-SWEEP-W{NEXT}, which must first give the 35 legacy rows keyed on the literal address a `signal-1` label, or adopting this marker there would unown them and silence ORPHAN across all 35.

Configures the reconciler's SOT_PARITY check — the one check that audits whether the DECLARATION each host reads is still the committed one, rather than reading it and assuming. Carries the SoT url, the enforcement mode (`report`) and a NUMERIC promotion criterion, so the report->block decision is a countable threshold rather than a judgement call held in someone's head. Missing or unparseable => the check reports COULD_NOT_COMPARE, never a pass. It is itself in declaration-sync.sh's synced set on purpose: the config for the check that detects stale declarations must not be a copy nobody keeps current. Deliberately covers ONLY monitoring-inventory.json — listing the other synced files here would duplicate a set already owned by that script's DECLARATIONS array, and a duplicated fact drifts.

The host-path claims made by the prescriptive docs, read by the reconciler's DOC_PATH_CLAIM check on the host that owns each claim. Closes the gap OPS-CLAUDEMD-CLAIM-VERIFIER-W1 shipped (9 claims UNPROBED behind --probe-hosts, unusable from CI). Existence is the ONE assertion the rest of this inventory delegates away: a DELETED artifact fires nothing (HASH_DRIFT skips what it cannot find, DARK needs a schedule, ORPHAN runs host->repo) - measured 2026-08-02 against send_telegram.sh.

SoT for CLAUDE.md's off-:00 cron law, with exactly TWO consumers and no third derivation: scripts/check-monitoring-schedules.mjs (authoring-time CI gate) and this inventory's own reconciler (the SCHEDULE_DRIFT authority hint). A JS gate cannot import a Python module, so the RULE DATA is the shared artifact and tests/unit/monitoring-schedule-boundary.test.ts pins both implementations to byte-identical verdicts over one fixture corpus. Installed on BOTH hosts because the reconciler runs once per host; a rule file present on only one would make the two hosts render the same drift differently, which is how send_telegram.sh sat behaviourally forked for 7 days.

exempt_consumers.detail: These use a zero-dep urllib send path by design, and that is CORRECT rather than tolerated. This wrapper carries ALERT semantics (severity-gated, 24h-deduped, operator-action-required); a per-fire INFO/WARN heartbeat is TELEMETRY, and CLAUDE.md already holds that a by-design fire has no meaningful cooldown threshold. Different contracts, different transports. Do NOT 'fix' these to route through the wrapper.

Small-n decline detector. Measured population at install: 10 charges lifetime, 1 failure, 4 subscriber rows — so a percentage would be an anecdote and a single-sample alarm is forbidden. TWO predicates: below MIN_N=20 only an ABSOLUTE FLOOR (>=3 distinct failed payments/7d) is live and the verdict is PASS carrying the observed n; at or above MIN_N the rate predicate activates with the floor still armed. Below MIN_N it is PASS, never INDETERMINATE — the WORLD builds this corpus, so empty is a fact, not a verification failure; the inverse would leave it permanently indeterminate, i.e. decoration. Every run appends its observed n to /var/lib/algovault-payment-decline/observations.jsonl so the MIN_N crossing RATE is measured rather than guessed at the decision. DECLINE_RATE_PCT_MAX=40 is an UNCALIBRATED PLACEHOLDER that structurally cannot fire below MIN_N: no honest calibration exists at n=10, and no published UnionPay cross-border benchmark exists to borrow. Whoever is present at the first MIN_N crossing owns calibrating it from the ledger. Verdict token PAYMENT_DECLINE_VERDICT= maps PASS=0/FAIL=1/INDETERMINATE=3; 3 is the token-law default for a NEW gate and must NOT be aligned to check-stripe-webhook-events.mjs's 2, which means a different thing in a different script.

UNBLOCKED 2026-08-12 by OPS-DRIFT-CANARY-INVOCATION-FIX-W1, which also CORRECTS this row's own prior root cause: of its three claims, two were wrong and the third was INVERTED. (1) 'the host checkout has the file but no node_modules' — irrelevant. build_nav.mjs imports only node: builtins and its transitive chain is entirely relative. The real host blocker is that dist/ is gitignored, and the host checkout's dist/ is a stale 2026-04-10 artifact carrying no lib/site-nav.js at all. (2) 'the prod image does not ship scripts/' — narrower than stated: the image ships 3 files under scripts/ (fetchers/, funnel-by-channel.mjs, refresh-knowledge-pages.mjs); what is absent is build_nav.mjs specifically. (3) 'its fail-open branch swallows rc=1 and exits 0' — INVERTED, and this is the consequential one. Line 41 read `[ "$RC" -ne 1 ]`, which swallows everything EXCEPT rc=1, while node's MODULE_NOT_FOUND throw exits exactly 1. Re-measured on signal-1 2026-08-12 under ALGOVAULT_TG_TEST_INERT=1: the canary reached its DRIFT branch and invoked send_telegram.sh, logging `DRIFT: served nav region out of sync with the model. ... Cannot find module '/app/scripts/build_nav.mjs'`. It was therefore never a dark guard — installed, it would have FALSE-PAGED every Tuesday with a body blaming a host-side HTML edit for a missing module. THE DEEPER DEFECT, which no invocation fix inside the container could reach: this canary's subject is the SERVED HTML, and Caddy serves the landing pages from the host webroot /var/www/algovault, not /app — and 10 of the 36 nav pages are absent from the image entirely. It now consumes the shared served-page checker ops/monitoring/served-region-check.mjs, which FETCHES each served page (the shape ops/cron/docs-drift-canary.sh already proved) and byte-compares it to the ONE canonical render (dist/lib/site-nav.js renderSiteNav(), reached over docker exec because the host dist/ is unusable). It emits SERVED_REGION_VERDICT=PASS|FAIL|INDETERMINATE (exit 0/1/3) and a cannot-check outcome ESCALATES rather than exiting 0. Coverage note: the PRIMARY gate (build_nav --check) already runs in deploy.yml, prepublishOnly and tests/build-nav.test.ts, so the unique coverage is post-deploy webroot mutation — real, not hypothetical: ops/cron/snapshot-landing-daily.sh runs `cp landing/*.html /var/www/algovault/` daily at 00:39 UTC.

THE ONE served-page region checker, consumed by both region drift canaries; a third region canary inherits the shape rather than adding a third copy. Retires the class 'a canary that inspects the BUILT artifact when its stated subject is the SERVED artifact' — see the nav-drift-canary and analytics-drift-canary rows for the measured defect and the inverted root cause it corrects. PLACEMENT: host_path is the REPO CHECKOUT, not /opt/algovault-monitoring, following the ops/cron/snapshot-landing-daily.sh precedent — it must read $REPO/landing/** to DERIVE its page set, so installing a second copy under /opt/algovault-monitoring would add a third sha256 to keep in sync without removing the cross-tree dependency. It therefore ships with the deploy's `git pull` and needs no installer step; HASH_DRIFT compares it against the same checkout the deploy materialises, and ops/cron/checkout-parity.sh already asserts that checkout is a clean ancestor of origin/main. NO own schedule: it is a library invoked by its two consumers, so the DARK check (which reads only rows carrying a schedule) correctly does not apply. `repo_resident: true` because host_path IS the repo copy — HASH_DRIFT skips such rows deliberately, since on the host both sides of that comparison come from the same checkout and reporting them in-sync would be a lie by construction. KNOWN GAP, recorded rather than papered over: nothing detects the host CHECKOUT being merely BEHIND origin/main — checkout-parity.sh's HEAD_UNMERGED check only catches a HEAD that is NOT an ancestor, so it passes on a stale-but-ancestral tree. SECRET HYGIENE: a keyed bucket's tracker_key IS the caller's av_free_ API key and is redacted by STRUCTURE (key:sha16:<digest>) in every log line and alert body; keyless free:v2:<hash> ids pass through.
